tapeLine: US stocks fell Monday after Trump rebuffed Iran's Hormuz proposal: the Dow lost 347.11 points (0.67%) to 51,481.51, the S&P 500 slid 0.77% to 7,683.69 and the Nasdaq Composite slipped 0.92% to 26,820.38, per TheStreet. The 10-year Treasury yield ended around 5.24% after touching 5.272%, a fresh 19-year high, per CNBC and Barchart-sourced market reports. WTI settled at $92.60 (+0.21%), per Capital Street FX; December gold fell 3.54% to $4,168.40, per the same report. The Dallas Fed's Texas manufacturing index eased to 9.8 in September from 11.6 in August, while its production index rose to 29.5 and input-price growth accelerated to 4.9%, the fastest in more than two years, per the Dallas Fed survey as reported by Seeking Alpha and Fort Worth Inc. Trump said Sunday he expects talks with Iran to resume this week through Qatari mediators, per CBS News and RFE/RL. Tuesday early trading showed Dow futures edging lower, per TheStreet.
matters:
Monday's session reversed Friday's relief. Stocks fell and the 10-year Treasury yield closed around 5.24%, a fresh 19-year high, as bond sellers returned after Trump rejected Iran's seven-day Hormuz proposal, per CNBC and TheStreet. The Fed-hike thread carried since 18 September is still open: Monday's Dallas Fed survey showed the headline index easing to 9.8 from 11.6 but production and new orders rising, with input-price growth at 4.9%, the fastest in more than two years, per the Dallas Fed as reported by Seeking Alpha.

The Iran thread moved from rejection to a possible resumption: Trump said Sunday he expects talks to resume this week and did not rule out further strikes before the midterms, per Fox News and CBS News. Tehran said it still expects a US response, per CBS News. No meeting or agreement has been reported.

The financing-desk thread is unchanged: CVC and NSSK's roughly $3.2bn (JPY500bn) preliminary, non-binding proposal for Kobayashi Pharmaceutical has no disclosed financing structure, and the largest shareholder Oasis is reported unlikely to back it, per Smartkarma and Private Equity Wire.

Invalidation: Tuesday's JOLTS and Conference Board confidence (both 10:00 ET), any confirmed resumption or collapse of US-Iran talks, and the 10-year yield's behaviour around 5.27% are the next tests.

regime.tag: Monday reversed Friday's relief rally as Trump's rejection of Iran's Hormuz plan sent the 10-year yield to a 19-year high and stocks and metals lower.
regime.sizing: The Fed-hike thread stays open, with the 28 October FOMC the decision point. The Iran thread moved from rejection toward possible resumed talks, unconfirmed. The financing-desk thread is unchanged.

secondOrder: Monday's WTI settle of $92.60 (+0.21%) shows the pre-market oil spike toward $96 did not hold, while the yield and equity moves did. That points to rates, not crude, as the main driver of Monday's selling, per the figures above. Gold's 3.54% drop alongside a rising yield fits the same reading; this is an observation, not a forecast.

scorecard.text: Monday's brief carried a pre-market read that WTI had jumped as much as 4% to $96.44 on reports that US-Iran talks had stalled. WTI settled at $92.60, up only 0.21%, and Trump said Sunday he expects talks to resume this week, per Capital Street FX and CBS News. The oil-spike and 'stalled talks' framing did not hold.
Monday's brief pointed to futures lower and the 10-year yield rising toward 5.23%. Stocks closed lower (S&P -0.77%) and the 10-year ended around 5.24%, per TheStreet and CNBC.

Monday's brief named the Dallas Fed index as a test: it came in at 9.8 versus 11.6 prior, with production and new orders higher, per Seeking Alpha. A mixed read for the Fed thread, which stays open. Any formal US response to Iran and any new Houthi strike on Saudi energy infrastructure remain unconfirmed.
